issue.title: Before-commit hook failure leaves the phase bead closed as done and strands the work in an ephemeral workspace with no marker
issue.description:
FOUND BY the sase-yf.3 land agent while verifying epic sase-yf.3. Phase bead sase-yf.3.2
was CLOSED with resolution `done` at 2026-09-08T22:14:12Z carrying a detailed verification
note ("just install passed ...; focused alias rendering tests passed (38); model-completion
PNG visual tests passed after updating and inspecting five alias scenarios; just check
passed; epic-symbol scan had no entries"). None of that work was ever on master. `git log
--all --grep=sase-yf` returns only the phase-1 commit 5620ac028 and the parent epic's
a95d7c1dd. The tree still had the pre-phase-2 strings (`Enter -> `, `Loading model
aliases...`) 12 hours later.

The whole phase-2 change — 9 files, +397/-8, plus 5 new PNG goldens — was sitting
uncommitted in the sibling ephemeral workspace
`.../workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_14`, whose HEAD was still 3ec9b78b2. The land agent
recovered it only because it read the source instead of trusting the phase note. Had
sase_14 been reclaimed or reused first, the work would have been unrecoverable.

Cause of the non-landing: `sase stitch create` ran its before-commit hook `just fix`, which
failed (exit 1) because the host-wide Cargo target `/mnt/poseidon/cargo-target` is 100%
full ("error: failed to create directory ... No space left on device (os error 28)"). The
finalizer then correctly declined to retry ("attempt 1's inputs -- repo HEAD, dirty-path
fingerprints, exclude set, and message digest -- are unchanged, so a retry is guaranteed to
fail identically") and preserved the commit message at
`<workspace>/.sase/finalizers/commit-message-1450554-1788905720581499420.txt`.

That much is arguably correct. The defect is what did NOT happen afterward:

1. sase-yf.3.2 was not reopened, and no note was appended to it recording that its stitch
   never landed. The bead's own record still asserts verified completion.
2. No task, notification, or gate was raised naming the stranded workspace, so nothing
   outside the failed run's transcript points at the uncommitted tree.
3. The epic runner advanced to the land agent as if the phase had landed.

The only durable trace is an `_ERROR`-suffixed chat transcript
(`sase chat show --basename gh_sase_org__sase-tmp_260908_172532-workflow_tmp_260908_172532_main_ERROR-260908_172536`)
plus a preserved commit-message file inside an ephemeral workspace clone.

Note the ordering constraint: per decision `host-owned-completion`, the agent closes its
bead inside its own turn and the host-owned commit finalizer runs afterward, so close can
never be gated on commit success. The repair therefore belongs on the failure side —
reopen the bead, or append a durable `STITCH FAILED:` note naming the workspace, commit
message path, and hook output — not on the close side.

Triage: searched all task statuses for `stitch create failed`, `before commit hook failed`,
`No space left on device`, and `stranded work`; swept every task bead created in the last
week; reviewed the 31 in-progress epic plans. Closest neighbours are all about the
AFTER-commit / push side, where a commit did land: sase-xi (resume pending stitch
hook-failure steps on finalizer retry), sase-yg (push failure records no unpushed-commit
marker), sase-ye (artifact-link index push never retried), sase-xj (after-commit hook
failure strands a shared repo mid-rebase). This report is the before-commit case, where
nothing was committed at all and the bead is the thing left lying. Active epic sase-yh
("Repair stitch recovery and retry unpublished artifact links", phase sase-yh.4 in
progress) is the natural future home for the repair, but it did not cause this — the hook
failed on disk space, not on origin reconciliation — so this is filed as a task with a
related link rather than as a DISCOVERED ISSUE note on sase-yh.

Size large: the right repair (reopen vs. durable bead note vs. a finalizer-owned
strandedwork record) and its interaction with the single-turn agent model need planning,
not a direct patch.

task_type_fields.impact:
Silent loss of completed, verified work, and a bead store that lies about it.

Concretely: 9 files (+397/-8) and 5 reviewed PNG goldens for epic sase-yf.3 phase 2 sat
uncommitted in workspace sase_14 for ~12 hours while the bead read `done`. The sase-yf.3
land agent recovered them by diffing sase_14 against master and replaying the patch, but
only because it re-read the source rather than trusting the phase note. Ephemeral `sase_<N>`
workspaces are recycled between agents, so the same failure with a slower land agent, or
with no land agent at all (a standalone task bead), loses the work outright.

Second-order damage: every downstream consumer of the bead store — epic progress, land
agents, `sase bead show`, the phase-completion checks that `sase bead close` enforces —
treats an unlanded phase as landed. The failure is invisible unless someone opens the
`_ERROR` chat transcript of a run nobody has a reason to open.
task_type_fields.location: builtin@commit finalizer / sase stitch create before-commit hook failure path; observed against phase bead sase-yf.3.2 and workspace clone sase_14
task_type_fields.repro:
Observed once, end to end, on 2026-09-08:

1. Fill (or otherwise break) the host-wide Cargo target so the repo's before-commit hook
   `just fix` exits non-zero. Here: `df -h /mnt/poseidon` reports 100% used, and
   `just fix` fails in `_setup` -> `rust-install` with
   `error: failed to create directory '/mnt/poseidon/cargo-target/release/.fingerprint/sase_core_py-...': No space left on device (os error 28)`.
2. Run an epic phase agent that finishes its work, closes its phase bead with
   `sase bead close <phase> --note "..."`, and declares a commit.
3. The host-owned commit finalizer runs `sase stitch create`, the before-commit hook
   fails, and the finalizer declines to retry because the inputs are unchanged.

Result: the phase bead stays CLOSED/`done` with its verification note intact, the epic
advances, and the entire change set remains uncommitted in the ephemeral workspace clone.
Reproduce the read side without re-running any of it:
`sase bead show sase-yf.3.2` (closed done, note claims full verification), then
`git log --all --grep=sase-yf` on sase master (only 5620ac028 and a95d7c1dd — no phase-2
commit), then
`sase chat show --basename gh_sase_org__sase-tmp_260908_172532-workflow_tmp_260908_172532_main_ERROR-260908_172536`
for the finalizer error and the preserved commit-message path.

payload.description: sase-yh is the active stitch-recovery epic and the natural home for this repair, but it did not cause this: the hook failed on disk space, not on origin reconciliation or resume
Same class on the other side of the commit: sase-yg is a push failure that records no unpushed-commit marker; this is a before-commit hook failure that records no marker at all
sase-xi resumes pending hook-failure steps when a commit already landed; this bug covers the before-commit case where nothing was committed and the bead is what is left stale

evidence.note: Independent reproduction by the sase-y5 land agent: phase sase-y5.10 closed as done at 2026-09-08T21:04Z, then its workflow stitch failed (before-commit hook just fix hit ENOSPC on /mnt/poseidon). Nothing marked the bead or epic; the tracked-file wiring edits were silently lost to later workspace resets and only untracked new files survived in a stash (recovered as artifact file:explicit:762a0fcfad720e2b70a9331b). Cost: a full medium phase must be re-implemented (child plan of sase-y5). The failure transcript is chat gh_sase_org__sase-tmp_260908_162033-workflow_tmp_260908_162033_main_ERROR-260908_162039.
